subject.title: [BUG] OpenAI Codex errors leak into user chat

question: Should OpenClaw silently drop unconfigured-provider/Codex failures at the provider/routing boundary, or normalize them into safe generic channel copy while preserving diagnostics?
rationale: The parser repair is narrow, but changing unconfigured-provider failures from visible generic copy to silent discard affects provider routing, observability, and user expectations for failed agent turns.

options.title: Fix parser and decide routing policy
options.body: Add `detail` parser/sanitizer coverage now, then land an explicit provider-routing rule for unconfigured-provider failures with tests and live proof.

options.title: Formatter-only repair
options.body: Only normalize `detail` payloads into generic safe copy and leave broader unconfigured-provider discard behavior for a separate product issue.

options.title: Close as covered by raw-error suppression
options.body: Treat the current generic raw-error fallback as sufficient and require a fresh live Telegram repro before changing routing behavior.

recommendation.title: Fix parser and decide routing policy
recommendation.body: Add `detail` parser/sanitizer coverage now, then land an explicit provider-routing rule for unconfigured-provider failures with tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the raw-provider-error delivery suppression path and is the clearest routing owner for deciding whether this becomes silent discard or generic user-facing copy.
